title: A lone tanker, 14 June 1944
eyebrow: Marianas lifeguard and Luzon Strait · BANG's second war patrol, in a pack with SEAHORSE and GROWLER

paras.text: BANG's first attack of her second patrol, on a tanker alone, as typed on her attack sheet. No Japanese record of it has been found yet.

BANG saw one hit forward of the stack, the tanker list and settle by the stern, and her crew put out boats; she claimed one 7,000–8,000-ton AO damaged. No Japanese record of the attack has been found. The Chichijima base force's June signal log has nothing for the 14th or 15th about a tanker torpedoed or her crew landed, only a Navy GHQ broadcast of a submarine "certainly present" at 1200 I at 22-30N 144-30E, four hours before BANG fired and some 80 nm east of her (p. 18) [[cite:jacar:C08030275500]]. The Navy's June summary has no entry for her either.

Positions are BANG's own dead reckoning and star sights; lines between them are straight, and where she went in between is not recorded. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position. As the clock passes each firing time a red ring pulses at BANG's position; hover a diamond for the attack sheet.

BANG kept zone K (−10) for Attack 1 and zone I (−9) for Attacks 2 and 3, as her report does; GROWLER kept I on station, but SEAHORSE kept H (−8). Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9): the escort division's chart has HI-67's two oilers hit at 1515, seven minutes after BANG's sheet.

No Japanese record has been found yet for Attacks 1 and 3; those actions show only the American side. Where the Japanese record names only the ships that were hit, the rest of the convoy is described as the boats saw it.

BANG's second war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74802784); SEAHORSE Patrol 5 (74845019); GROWLER Patrol 9 (74818866). The 1st Surface Escort Division war diary, June 1944, via JACAR (C08030141000, National Institute for Defense Studies). Sarawak Maru's record from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

events.words: Navy GHQ signal 141730: 14th, 1200, 22-30N 144-30E, other (type of report): presence of an enemy submarine certain
events.original: 大海機密第一四一七三〇番電 十四日一二〇〇 二二─三〇N 一四四─三〇E 其ノ他 敵潜ノ存在確実
events.translation: Navy GHQ signal 141730: 14th, 1200, 22-30N 144-30E, other (type of report): presence of an enemy submarine certain
events.note: Chichijima Area Special Base Force war diary, June 1944, part 2 (its signal log, 令達報告等): a Navy GHQ broadcast (大海, 一般) sent at 1730 and logged at 1744 on the 14th (read at 400 dpi). It is the signal J06's table row was entered from, and its figures are clear where the table's are not: 1200, not 1600 or 1700, and 22-30N. So the report is from four hours before BANG fired (1601 I) and about 80 nm east of her attack position: not her attack. "Other" is not explained; it is not a torpedoing. The log for the 14th and 15th (pp17-20) has no tanker torpedoed and no survivors landed: its other submarine reports are direction-finding fixes from the Owada station and an attack on the Miho Maru convoy near 29N 141E. Zone not stated; taken as I, assumed

events.title: BANG
events.note: Zone I (Tokyo time) assumed: the note writes no zone letter, and the matched notes bear it out. The position is read off the map from where the mark sits (about ±0.1–0.3°), not the note's. Green circle; the name is hard to read. 1210 I = 1310 K, when BANG was on the surface making an end-around on the tanker (surfaced 1140 K, dived 1549 K). Measured against the bold 20N and 140E lines

words.type_attack: Day periscope attack. Fired three torpedoes using 1½° between torpedoes applied from aft forward by means of the offset knob on TDC. Kept constant periscope bearings to TDC during firing.
words.description: Empty tanker. Nearest estimate SYOYO MARU, page 286, ONI 208-J (revised), except he had a short heavy goal post between foremast and bridge structure. Estimate certain.
words.determined_by: Saw and heard one hit forward of stack. Saw target list and settle by stern, and put out life boats.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 14' (light) Course: 044° Speed: 10 (At firing) Range: 3600
words.remarks: Nine foot depth set because of rough sea conditions. Believe a shallower depth would have caused more damage on empty tanker.
words.note: Gyro angles are typed relative to the bow (10R, 8R, 6R), not as true gyro angles as on the other sheets; with own course 080 and target course 044 they give the typed tracks (134P, 136P, 138P). Tube 1 (Mark 23) has power typed "-". The Mark 14-3A entries for tubes 2 and 3 are circled by hand on the scan. The longitude's last characters are cut off at the scan's edge (143°-15.6E in positions.csv).
